nodes.label: Module 13 — eMAR & Medication Administration
nodes.rationale: Hospice nurses give doses at 3 AM in a patient's bedroom while the family watches; the captured record is the only evidence that survives, so the bet is that bedside capture quality translates directly to patient safety and survey defensibility.

nodes.label: administration_record Spine with mode Discriminator (D1, D11)
nodes.rationale: The eMAR is always projected across M12 + M13, never stored — a materialized view goes stale the moment M12 mutates (order correction, discharge cascade). IV-continuous is a sequence of rows sharing iv_session_id rather than one mutable-rate row, because a mutable rate would violate append-only audit and mismatch the FHIR mapping.

nodes.label: Scheduled-Dose Materialization from sigStructured (D2)
nodes.rationale: Pre-computing puts the schedule on a query-friendly index the missed-dose sweep needs; computing on read is non-trivial across DST transitions and named-time frequencies. Past scheduled-dose rows are immutable — their existence as a 'should have happened at 0800' record is the survey-defensible trail against which administrations and misses reconcile.

nodes.label: 15-Minute Missed-Dose Detection Sweep (D4)
nodes.rationale: A per-row delayed job would put 100k+ jobs in flight at a 30-patient census; a bounded idempotent polling sweep recovers gracefully from worker outage. Detecting within 15 minutes gets the case manager an alert while there is still time to act, versus competitors' daily batch report read at QAPI a week later.

nodes.label: Controlled-Substance Witness via Separate-Device HMAC Token (D7, M13-F04)
nodes.rationale: UI-checkbox witness implementations are known to be bypassed by the clinician clicking both attestations; a separate device, session and identity is the only audit-defensible pattern. Per ADR-0019 the mandate is scoped to waste/disposal and inpatient administration — routine in-home administration by a lone clinician records the clinician's attestation plus controlled-substance accounting rather than a fabricated second witness.

nodes.label: Comfort-Kit Deployment & Per-Medication Drawdown (D5)
nodes.rationale: The clinical record of what was used from a patient's kit is M13's domain (it is the administration trail) while physical replenishment is M21's fulfillment workflow. Competitors never reconcile the two, so a surveyor asking how the morphine in the kit was used gets a paper log from the family.

nodes.label: Medication Reconciliation as a Workflow, Not a Screen (D17)
nodes.rationale: Vendors implement reconciliation as a static form whose decisions do not structurally back-link to the resulting orders, so 'show me why this order was carried forward from home meds' gets a free-text answer. Per-line decision rows back-linking to the M12 order the prescriber signs make survey reconstruction deterministic.

nodes.label: Offline Capture Queue with administeredAt vs recordedAt (D18)
nodes.rationale: Requiring connectivity pushes rural nurses to paper and breaks the timestamp trail. The clinician's wall-clock administeredAt is preserved as truth, recordedAt is server-receive, idempotency is keyed on (orgId, deviceId, localId), and the sync path re-checks M12 state so an administration against a since-discontinued order surfaces as a workflow item rather than being silently accepted or silently dropped.

nodes.label: Bidirectional Consistency: M13 Asks M12 at Every Write (D6)
nodes.rationale: The data dependency runs M13 → M12 (an administration is meaningless without its order), so inverting into an M12→M13 cascade would force M12 to know M13's schema and active-administration set. A synchronous getAdministrationContext consult inside the route handler is simpler, atomic and correct; a soft advisory check is inadequate for clinical safety.

nodes.label: Server-Side Five-Rights Validation
nodes.rationale: Patient, drug (RxNorm crosswalk), dose, route and time are each validated against the order and the scheduled dose at write; mismatches return 422 FIVE_RIGHTS_VIOLATION naming the specific right that failed.

nodes.label: PRN Effectiveness Reassessment Trigger (M13 triggers, M9 scores — D3)
nodes.rationale: Splitting responsibility avoids M13 carrying scale-licensing logic and M9 carrying administration-lifecycle logic; M9 could not originate the trigger without subscribing to M13 anyway. Vendors' free-text 'effectiveness' box is rarely completed, never trended and never tied to a scale that measures effectiveness.

nodes.label: Caregiver-Attested Administration with requires_rn_review (D10)
nodes.rationale: Caregivers give doses and documenting the fact is clinically and legally meaningful, but it is not the same accountability chain as clinician administration; routing it to the same cosign queue as M8 LPN/CHHA notes keeps the RN's 'things requiring my review' unified across modules.

nodes.label: AI-Prohibited Zone for Medication Administration (D15)
nodes.rationale: Extends M12's prescribing-side block to the administration side: an LLM cannot create a fake administration to mask diversion, cannot witness a controlled-substance dose, and cannot adjust a five-rights violation. HearthNote Layer 2 may narrate around an administration in read-only context only.
